# 0024. The provenance record splits normative hashes from a descriptive environment

## Status

Accepted. Date: 2026-11-12. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-hephkit-lab-research-core-design.md` §9.1, §9.2.1.

## Context

`spec/heph-spec.md` §7 has carried a provenance record since `0.1.0`, marked **draft**, with five fields — `run_id`, `config_hash`, `data_hash`, `code_sha` and `class` — and a note that the fields may change before promotion. [ADR 0022](/adrs/0022-research-integrity-is-the-spine) made that record the spine of `hephkit.lab` rather than a convenience, so the draft has to become something an implementation can be held to before `lab.repro` is written against it.

Two facts the record does not yet hold have to go in. The parent design, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-hephaestus-design.md`, asks `lab.repro` to capture the dependency lockfile hash and the GPU driver. Adding both as plain fields is the naive fix and it breaks the thing being built. The record's five existing fields are all *normative*: they are what a replay compares, so a difference in any of them means the replay is not the same run. Put the GPU driver in that set and the same configuration, data and code re-executed on a second machine stops matching. `deterministic` would then be a label nothing could ever wear, because no two machines agree on their driver version, and a class that is unreachable in practice is decoration.

The lockfile hash does not have that problem. Two different dependency sets genuinely give different answers, so a replay against a different lockfile *is* a different run and should be reported as one.

So the two additions are not the same kind of thing, and the record needs a distinction it does not currently have.

A second question sits underneath. If `deterministic` is reachable, what makes a run eligible for it? The draft said nothing, which left an implementation free to stamp `deterministic` on a run from a dirty working tree with no lockfile — a record that claims re-execution while naming neither the code nor the dependencies that produced the result.

## Decision

**Fields split by whether they decide reproducibility or merely describe it.** Spec §7.1 names a **determinism contract**: `config_hash`, `data_hash`, `deps_hash` and `code_sha`. `run_id` identifies the run and `class` classifies it, so neither is in the contract. `environment` is descriptive, and §7.2 says normatively that a replay MUST NOT compare it and that two records differing only in `environment` are not a divergence. That sentence, not a column in a table, is what keeps the label wearable: the distinction has to be a rule an implementer in another language can satisfy, not an inference a reader draws from a layout.

**`deps_hash` is normative and is a hash of the lockfile.** It is a content hash (spec §4.2) over the lockfile's bytes exactly as read, not over a parsed form, because a lockfile is not required to be JSON and §4.1's canonicalisation therefore does not apply to it. It is `null` exactly when the run had no lockfile.

**`environment` carries `platform`, `python`, `frameworks` and `accelerator`, and never an identifier of a person or a machine. My call, taken by the user.** Hostname, username and filesystem paths are excluded under any member name. [ADR 0022](/adrs/0022-research-integrity-is-the-spine) makes `lab.gates` require records to be committed and citable, which means they are published alongside a paper; spec §6.2 already requires `pii: true` attributes to be redacted from log output, and a researcher's machine name or home directory in a permanent public artefact is the same class of thing as one in a log line, only harder to withdraw. A project that wants them carries them in its own configuration, outside the record. An absent framework is recorded as `null` rather than omitted, so the record distinguishes "looked for and not there" from "never asked".

**A run is `provenance-only` unless a git commit names its code, the working tree is clean and a lockfile exists.** The clean tree and the lockfile are the user's decisions, not derivations; the commit condition, which §7.3 lists first, is settled in the paragraph after this one. A dirty tree means the commit `code_sha` names is no longer the code that ran, which is the one job `code_sha` has in the record — the SHA is still recorded, the label is not. No lockfile means no `deps_hash` and so an unpinned dependency set. Failing any one of the three costs the label and nothing else: the run is still recorded in full, with `config_hash`, `data_hash`, `environment` and whichever hashes it can produce, so a marimo session or a conda environment gets an honest `provenance-only` and loses no traceability.

**A run whose code no git commit names is the same shape of case, so it is settled the same way: `code_sha` is `null`, and the run is `provenance-only`.** This is another precondition on the label rather than a refusal to record. The first draft of §7 left it unstated, on the grounds that inventing a null form for `code_sha` was beyond the question being decided; that was wrong, and the hole is closed in §7 rather than relocated to a later section. §7.1 made `code_sha` a required non-null string, bound the clean-tree test to `git status --porcelain`, and forbade omitting a required member, which together left an implementation outside a git tree with no conforming record to write at all. The nullable `code_sha` is no more an invention than the nullable `deps_hash` decided above, and it is the same reasoning: a hash the run cannot produce is recorded as absent and costs the label, never the record. It also gives `lab.repro` a spec to implement against, since a missing repository must degrade to `provenance-only` rather than raise.

The condition is anchored to **naming a git commit**, not to being in a version-controlled tree, because the second phrasing leaves holes that the first closes in one clause. A git repository with no commit yet is a version-controlled tree with no SHA to record, and a Mercurial tree is version-controlled while the field is a git commit SHA and the clean test is `git status --porcelain`, so neither could ever produce a conforming value under the looser wording. §7 therefore states outright that it names code by a git commit, and ties the field to whether `HEAD` resolves: a dirty tree keeps its non-null `code_sha` and loses only the label, which is what §7.3's clean-tree precondition already implied and what `lab.repro` needs on the busiest path there is. That is honest about what this repository is: git throughout, with tooling that assumes it. A VCS-agnostic code identifier would be an invention nothing here would use, and the alternative — leaving a Mercurial tree formally unable to write a record — is worse than naming the assumption.

"Clean" is resolved into a condition an implementation can check: nothing tracked differs from the commit named by `code_sha`, and no untracked file is present other than those the repository's ignore rules exclude — a tree for which `git status --porcelain` prints nothing. The stricter reading is deliberate. An untracked script that the run imported is code that ran and is not in `code_sha`, which is the exact failure the precondition exists to prevent, so untracked files dirty the tree too.

**`data_hash`'s digest scope is deferred to §10, and §7 says so.** Whether that hash runs over raw bytes or canonical JSON, and how a multi-file dataset combines into one value, belongs with dataset manifests; the design's §9.2 assigns it there. Leaving it merely unstated next to a `deps_hash` whose scope §7 settles precisely would read as an omission rather than a deferral, and an implementer in another language would fill it in differently from ours. §7.1 therefore names the question and points at §10.

**Hashing the resolved installed distribution set instead of the lockfile was considered and rejected.** It varies by platform and by CUDA build at the same version string, which smuggles the environment back into the contract this ADR exists to keep it out of.

**`provenance-only` is hyphenated, and the hyphen is normative.** Nocturna, one of the harvest sources, spells it `provenance_only`; that is a divergence, recorded here so nobody adopts it by copying.

**The spec moves to `0.5.0`.** §7 loses its draft status and gains MUST sentences where it previously had none. [ADR 0019](/adrs/0019-the-public-domain-is-hephkit-dev) settled that a changed MUST is a minor bump, so this is one. `0.4.0` is taken by the idempotency change in §2, so this is `0.5.0`, and the `spec` field of every conformance vector and the `const` in `conformance/schema/vector-file.schema.json` move with it. The rest of this wave's spec work lands in the same `0.5.0`.

**Four codes enter `spec/errors.yaml` under area `LAB`:** `HEPH-LAB-422` (experiment config failed validation), `HEPH-LAB-409` (replay diverged from its record), `HEPH-LAB-424` (a required record, manifest or frozen input is missing) and `HEPH-LAB-412` (an integrity gate failed). They are the set the design's §9.4 settles; no code is added speculatively ahead of the module that raises it.

## Consequences

`deterministic` is now strict rather than unwearable, and it is earnable exactly where the discipline already exists. This repository, SAWA and NeoRx all run under git with a `uv.lock`, so runs there can claim it; everything else gets `provenance-only`, which is an honest answer and not a degraded one. The failure mode this protects against is the opposite of the obvious one: the risk was never that too few runs would qualify, it was that a label attached to every run would stop meaning anything.

The split has a cost in what the record can tell you. A replay that matches on all four contract members but produced a different number has to be explained by something outside the contract, and `environment` is where the reader looks — descriptively, by hand. `lab.replay` cannot do that reasoning, by construction, because the moment it compares `environment` the contract has grown the field this ADR removed from it. `HEPH-LAB-409`'s developer guidance therefore sends the reader to the difference report rather than to a re-run.

`environment` is an open object whose named members are individually optional but whose names and types are reserved, so a project may add members and an implementation on another runtime may omit `python`, while nobody may record a platform under a second name. That is deliberate — implementations differ in what they can see — and it is also the place this decision can rot: the exclusion of hostname, username and paths is a prose MUST in §7.5 with no check behind it, and nothing in `tools/` can see a hostname smuggled in under another member name. The guard is review of the module that builds the record, and a vector for `lab.provenance.record` once the design's §9.3 suite exists.

Two questions are deliberately left to other sections, and both are pointed at from §7 rather than left silent. `data_hash`'s digest scope is section 10's, with dataset manifests. And §7.2 constrains only that a replay never compares `environment` — what a replay does compare, and what "identical result" means for floating point, belong to spec §9 and are not decided here.

**Three cases §7 deliberately does not answer**, recorded so that a later reader knows they were seen and left: which repository's commit `code_sha` names when the code is in a **submodule**; code assembled from **two repositories**, which a single `code_sha` string cannot express; and a commit that exists **only locally and was never pushed**, where the SHA is valid and resolvable to nobody but the person who ran it. None needs a change to §7 as written, and each would be a spec change if it were ever answered.

Two narrower things are not settled by anything yet. §7.3 tests its preconditions "when the run starts", which means the class cannot be verified from the record alone after the fact, and says nothing about a tree dirtied mid-run. Both are judged the right trade for a record that has to be written before the work finishes, and both are carried forward to the replay section and the `lab.provenance.record` vectors rather than widened here.

The `0.5.0` bump re-stamps twelve vector files and the schema `const` alongside them in the same commit as the §7 revision, which is the whole point of doing it here: leaving the spec revised while it still declared `0.4.0` would make one version number name two different specifications mid-branch. `tools/gen_idempotency_vectors.py` and `tools/gen_signature_vectors.py` each hold the version as a constant and were moved with it, or the next run of either would quietly revert the stamp.
